I've had problems with ubuntu in the past, and zorin is just kinda half assed ubuntu with a nice UI that I could never set up a VPN on.

I don't care about size or anything, although I guess faster is better.
Can someone recommend a good dist with a lot of functionality, easy to use, and I can set up openVPN on without any trouble?

Easy to use and lots of functionality don't always go hand in hand. Ubuntu would have been my first recommendation but if you had problems with it you can also check out OpenSUSE and Fedora. Of the two I know Fedora a bit better and would recommend it over OpenSUSE. Korora, a Fedora derivative, aims to be user friendly and working out of the box with a couple of choices for desktop environments. https://kororaproject.org
Settimg up openvpn on openSUSE is not really straight forward because it doesn't use networkmanager by default.

I used to use Kubuntu but I experienced DNS leaks while using Networkmanager and openvpn, the bug is still open/unresolved. I decided to try out an easy Arch based distro. I chose Netrunner Rolling which is based on Manjaro , and haven't had any problems. So I'd recommend all three of these.

I have openVPN running on a mint desktop and laptop. Took some tweaking because the VPN vendor had shit documentation. I do not attribute this to weaknesses in Linux but to lack of interest in supporting anything beyond MS and Mac.

It is nice, I can switch from wifi to VPN with a slide of a virtual switch.

OpenVPN is a tad problematic to install, other programs must be installed with it. Enter "sudo apt-get install network-manager-openvpn-gnome" in any Ubuntu system. This command will install all you need for openVPN.
